newsitem.title: USA: Keystone to buy Financial Trust for $371 million.
newsitem.headline: Keystone to buy Financial Trust for $371 million.

text.p: Keystone Financial Inc. said Friday it has agreed to acquire Financial Trust Corp., another Pennsylvania banking company, for about $371 million.
The news sent Financial Trust stock up over 36 percent, gaining $10.75 to $40 a share on Nasdaq in late morning trading. Keystone stock fell $1 to $25.75, also on Nasdaq.

Under the agreement, each Financial Trust share will be converted into 1.65 shares of Keystone. Based on Thursday's $26.50 per share closing bid price of Keystone, Carlisle, Pa.-based Financial Trust is worth about $43.73 per share or $371 million.
Financial Trust, a bank holding company with four member banks and about $1.2 billion in assets, operates 48 community offices in seven counties in Pennsylvania and Maryland.
Keystone, the fifth-largest banking company in Pennsylvania, has five member banks which operate 147 offices in Pennsylvania, Maryland and West Virginia.
Financial Trust Chief Executive Ray Wolfe will become Keystone's chairman and join its board with two other Financial Trust directors, the company said.

Keystone based in Harrisburg, Pa., said after the merger and the previously announced acquisition of First Financial Corp. of Western Maryland, its assets will increase 30 percent to about $6.7 billion.
